We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (each a tuple). Need to choose one that can be further processed with next template 1914389, then 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

We attempted applying 1914389 to some of those, got some results for one: applying to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" gave result with two products: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". That seems like a disconnection: maybe the template splits a silyl protected group? Not sure.

We need to continue chain: after 1914389 we need to apply 1914390 to each product? Actually the route is linear: each reaction uses a template to go from product to precursors. So we need a tree where each node is a molecule, each reaction node has children precursors. The sequence of templates must be applied in order from target downwards.

Thus we need to construct a retrosynthesis tree of depth 5 (5 reactions). Starting with target (level0). Reaction1 uses template 29646, giving some precursors (maybe 3). Then for each of those, we apply template 1914389 to each (maybe only one branch continues). Then apply 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

We need to find applicable precursors at each step. We have some results but not all.

Let's examine the result of template 29646: It returned three tuples each containing a SMILES string. The result format: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C',))"

Actually the result shows three separate tuples each with one SMILES. Let's parse:

1. "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO"
2. "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C"
3. "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)"

The third seems like a simpler fragment lacking the silyl group and side chain. Might be the core.

We need to apply template 1914389 to each. We tried on the first two (with silyl) and got a result for the first? Actually we applied to the first with silyl? We applied to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" (which is similar but missing silyl on the acid). That gave result with two products: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". So template 1914389 seems to split off a side chain (maybe a phosphonate). Good.

Now we need to apply template 1914390 to each of those precursors? The order says after 1914389, we apply 1914390. So we need to take each product from 1914389 and apply 1914390. We attempted applying 1914390 to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and got no result. Also applied to "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC" and got no result.

Maybe we need to choose a different precursor from 29646 that works with 1914389 then 1914390 etc.

Let's try applying 1914389 to the third precursor "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)".
